summary: Derive discardable clump envelopes and material-coordinate samples from solved graph memberships.
x-representation: For each graph clump, sample member positions at common fractional intrinsic distances. A transported frame and member covariance define elliptical cross-sections; member coordinates in those frames retain the solved population. Convergence holds split incoming and outgoing spans. The shell is derived display only, never an authored surface or a strand-generation primitive.
x-budget: At most 65 rings and 12 shell vertices per ring per clump; 256 numerical members. Report logical population separately from evaluated sample counts. Flat diagnostic colours identify sections.
x-contact: Project derived shell vertices against the same worker-owned collision fields; member identities and solved lengths do not change.
x-tests: Deterministic frames and membership, finite bounded buffers, exact reconstruction of member samples, conservation through convergence and no modification of authored graph or solved paths.
x-hierarchy: New grooms partition each major section into sixteen stable two-dimensional root-chart clumps. The display preserves section hue and varies lightness per clump. Covariance envelopes have a diagnostic tip taper; they are approximate spread displays, not containment bounds. Existing authored graphs are retained.
